_comment: Row 214 battery: a zombie in a just-exited tracer's group is an uncollected exit status, not residue. Re-run: toolchain/bin/bd-mutate --spec tests/mutants/writerec_zombie_residue.json --work DETACHED_SCRATCH. Reasoning that cannot live on a mutant: M1 is the defect itself -- one killpg reading, which succeeds for a zombie, deciding permanently. M2 is the mutant that matters, because a fix that only made the false refusal go away would be indistinguishable from deleting the check; it must be caught by a LIVE process still being terminated and reported. M3 pins fail-closed: an unreadable /proc is residue, never innocence. M4 pins the race the census itself introduces -- the group can drain between the probe and the walk, and without the re-probe the fix reproduces the defect one window later. M5 is an overcorrection rather than a regression: it is CORRECT and it is the draft's shape, so only the cost-structure test can see it -- 39ms per /proc walk over 856 pids on test5, against 0.003ms for the killpg probe. NOT INCLUDED: SETTLE_SECONDS -> 0.0, which is near-equivalent because the census still rescues the zombie case. BAND: this file only. The end-to-end residual path (a real strace tracer handing back a live group) is pinned by M13/M14 of tests/mutants/v3_66_1194_write_recorder.json, whose band is that suite.
subject: row 214 -- bd-writerec must not refuse a correct capture over a zombie

mutants.label: M1 judge the group on the killpg reading alone, as before row 214
M2 launder a running process into the residue states
M3 skip a /proc entry that cannot be read instead of refusing (fail open)
M4 drop the post-census re-probe, so a group that drained mid-census is signalled
M5 move the /proc census onto the polling path (the draft's shape)
